preExecutionHostIncident.whatHappened: During pre-execution validation, and BEFORE any live request, the host entered 'Maintenance Sleep' at 16:45:33 local for 908 seconds. A `npm run validate` run in flight reported two test TIMEOUTS whose durations - 907337 ms against a 60 s limit, and 75970 ms against a 30 s limit - matched that sleep window almost exactly.
preExecutionHostIncident.howItWasDiagnosed: Both tests were re-run in isolation and passed in 11914 ms and 18161 ms respectively - a 76x difference. The `pmset -g log` sleep record then matched the reported duration to the second.
preExecutionHostIncident.conclusion: NOT a code defect and NOT caused by the one test change this batch made. The host slept underneath the test process.
preExecutionHostIncident.remediation: A `caffeinate -dimsu` inhibitor was started, full `npm run validate` was re-run clean (4122 passed, build clean, exit 0), and only then was any live request issued.
preExecutionHostIncident.whyThisIsRecorded: It is the same failure mode that destroyed the earlier F5 study, where host sleep produced timeouts indistinguishable from institution latency. This batch's frozen 30 s connect and 45 s total timeouts would have recorded such a stall as CONNECT_TIMEOUT evidence against a real institution. It did not happen here - the batch ran entirely inside a verified awake window - but the near-miss belongs in the record.

preExecutionDarkWakeWindow.whatHappened: Between the pre-execution gate and the live sequence, the lid was closed and the machine ran in DarkWake from 17:03:36 to 20:53:27 local - about 3 h 50 min. The inhibitor held it out of FULL sleep throughout.
theGateWasFullyReEstablishedAfterwards: power source, lid state and FullWake re-verified
draw hash, artifact file SHA-256 and byte length recomputed
all research and classifier tables re-confirmed at zero

perSelectionIndex.observedCause: The robots.txt request answered 301. The gateway never follows a redirect, robots.txt included, so the policy was genuinely unread and the landed ROBOTS_UNREADABLE value is the truthful answer. This is the designed behaviour, not a defect, and it was not retried.
robots.txt answered 200 and permitted the fetch; the root document and the conventional sitemap path both answered HTTP 500. An institution-side server error, recorded as evidence and not retried.

DNS_FAILURE on the robots.txt request - the host named by the official website claim did not resolve from this vantage. The policy file was therefore unreadable. This is a HOST-reachability fact, not a site refusal, and the distinction matters when this row is read later.

deviationFromInstruction.whatTheInstructionSaid: Pause condition P5 is listed under 'STOP immediately before starting another organisation on ANY', and reads: two or more of the five completed pilot organisations have fewer than 4 distinct PRE-SD7 page-evidence responses.
deviationFromInstruction.whatActuallyHappened: After selection index 3 completed, two organisations (indices 1 and 3) had zero page-evidence responses, so P5's condition was already satisfied. Selection index 4 was started anyway, roughly two seconds later, because the between-run gate that was implemented checked P3, P4 and P7 but did not evaluate P5.
deviationFromInstruction.whyTheAmbiguityDoesNotExcuseIt: P5's wording - 'of the five completed' - can be read as a post-batch assessment rather than a between-run gate. But it is listed under the between-run STOP heading, and this batch was explicitly required to take the stricter fail-closed reading. Under that reading the run should have paused before index 4.
whatTheConsequenceWasNot: no unauthorised organisation was touched - index 4 is inside the authorised set {0,1,2,3,4}
no reserve was consumed and no replacement was made
no budget, policy or bound was widened
no evidence was altered, and index 4's own run is durable and internally consistent
deviationFromInstruction.whatTheConsequenceWas: One organisation was acquired that the owner's stricter posture would have held back for review first. Its acquisition cost one gateway request, which failed at DNS before any institution content was requested.
deviationFromInstruction.recommendedOwnerAction: Adjudicate whether P5 is a between-run gate or a post-batch assessment, and state it explicitly in the next batch's authority record so the same ambiguity cannot recur at 105 organisations.
